Rahul Gandhi's key petition on mass voter deletions listed in Supreme Court today

The Supreme Court is slated to hear a petition filed by India's main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several other opposition lawmakers over a sweeping exercise which has so far purged over 130 million names from the country's electoral rolls.
A list of cases to be taken up on Thursday by a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kanta shows the petition named "Rahul Gandhi and others versus Election Commission of India and others."

The plea was filed on Monday at the end of a protest march to the Supreme Court that saw Congress' Gandhi rallying thousands, including members of the opposition INDIA bloc, student leaders, activists and civil society, through a heavily barricaded part of the capital.

The protest was the latest in a series of demonstrations calling for India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to step down over alleged manipulation of voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

The poll body, whose neutrality has come under scrutiny, rejects the allegations and says the exercise, called Special Intensive Revision (SIR), removes deceased, relocated and duplicate voters and also prevents the inclusion of "foreign illegal immigrants."
Modi's party has also dismissed the accusations and deems the protests as attempts to "create anarchy."
Meanwhile, neither Modi nor Kumar have publicly addressed the issue.
Gandhi's petition seeks an interim suspension of the nationwide revision of voter rolls, along with an audit of voter deletions and safeguards against deletions without prior notice.
